title: Staged readiness filter & region-aware derating to stabilize autoscaler
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement: Over the last quarter we've observed frequent autoscaler oscillations in multi-region clusters when transient probe failures (readiness/liveness) or short-lived tail-latency spikes coincide with bursty traffic. These scale events trigger downstream routing churn, risk SLO violations during cool-down windows, and increase cost. Current readiness checks are binary and applied uniformly across regions which makes the autoscaler hypersensitive to noise and regional transient degradation.

Goal: Implement a 'staged readiness filter' that aggregates per-instance health signals with short-term smoothing and region-aware derating so the autoscaler reacts to sustained capacity needs while preserving fast failure detection for true outages. Targets: reduce scale-up/scale-down oscillations by >=60% in load tests, and keep 99th-percentile request latency under 250ms during failover windows.

Scope and non-goals: This ticket covers runtime probe processing, autoscaler input transformation, and rollout controls in the control plane. It does NOT include full client-side routing changes or downstream SLA changes (those are separate).

Proposed design (high level):
- Readiness smoothing layer: maintain a short windowed score per replica (exponential moving average of pass/fail + latency health). Probe result = weighted combination of success rate, recent p95 latency, and recent error-rate.
- Staged readiness states: healthy | degraded | marginal | offline. Only transition to 'offline' after sustained failures beyond hysteresis thresholds. 'Degraded' and 'marginal' influence autoscaler differently (e.g., mark replica as reduced capacity rather than fully unavailable).
- Region-aware derating: when a region's error budget burn or probe failure rate exceeds configured thresholds, mark the region in an elevated-derate mode where autoscaler uses conservative scaling (larger cool-downs, scaled-down weight for ephemeral probes) and routing control plane can shift traffic gradually to healthy regions.
- Circuit breaker integration: tie cluster-level circuit breakers to the aggregated health score (not raw probes). If cluster health score degrades, open short-lived circuit breakers to shed low-priority work (batch/async) and preserve capacity for high-priority requests.
- Autoscaler input adaptation: replace raw readiness counts with a capacity-weighted effective replica count computed from staged readiness. The autoscaler will consider effective throughput capacity and not just replica count.
- Telemetry and safety: add a control-plane flag (staged-readiness.enabled) and canary rollout with traffic % and a revert API. Metrics to add: effective_replica_count, staged_state_transitions, region_derate_factor, autoscale_action_reason (probe-noise|sustained-load|manual), and incident boolean.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Simpler binary readiness is fast but noisy; smoothing reduces noise at the cost of longer detection windows. We balance by using staged states with retention tuned to keep detection for true crashes fast (offline detection still short) while smoothing transient latency/errors.
- Region derating introduces complexity in control plane routing decisions; we limit surface area by only modifying autoscaler inputs and emitting signals for the existing routing layer to act on separately.
- Conservative autoscaler behavior risks underprovisioning during sustained spikes; to mitigate, we add a burst-capacity policy and a fast-path for explicit scale-up requests from monitoring alerts.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Prototype smoothing and staged-state computation in runtime agent (unit tests + synthetic probe harness) - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1429
2) Autoscaler consumer change to accept effective_replica_count + reason annotations; add metric exports - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/386
3) Region derating policy + circuit breaker hook in control plane; add Grafana panels and alert rules - Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Staged+Readiness+Design, Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime/autoscale-health
4) Integration tests with chaos monkey (probe flaps, region partition) and HTTPerf load profiles to validate oscillation reduction
5) Canary rollout to 5% clusters, monitor 48h, expand to 50% then global if metrics pass

Acceptance criteria:
- Load test scenario (planned burst) shows >=60% fewer scale actions over 6-minute windows compared to baseline
- 99p latency remains <250ms and error-rate stays within SLO during canary window
- No increase in Mean Time To Detect (MTTD) of true host crashes beyond documented threshold (design target: offline detection <= 20s)

Safety & revert: Feature flag gate, emergency toggle to revert to binary readiness, automated alert if autoscale flapping increases above baseline within canary window.

Operational notes: Configure default hysteresis and smoothing window per-instance to 5–12s depending on tier (low-latency tiers have shorter windows). Default region-derate threshold is 5% error budget burn in 1m.
